calculation_notes: All usage quantities are filled with the planning assumptions above; the total is a budget, not a measured invoice or a forecast of indefinite data growth.

Hourly SKU amounts use quantity x hourly rate x allocated hours. Monthly capacity/VPU SKU amounts use quantity x monthly rate x allocated hours / 744. Scratch uses 62 hours; other monthly storage inputs are monthly average retained quantities over 744 hours.
Request quantity is in units of 10,000 requests. Gross prices exclude discounts, credits and tax; the OCI estimator may recalculate account/free-tier deductions on import.
Database storage is shared across each three-node system; node replication does not multiply the modeled storage quantity. Standard E5 compute and the PostgreSQL service fee are separate charges.

Object storage, application backups, Gitaly snapshots and managed PostgreSQL backups represent separate data populations; no application backup is counted again as a managed database or volume snapshot.
Two load balancers have 2 base-instance units and 350 aggregate weighted-average Mbps units; the real deployed limits remain 100–1000 Mbps per LB.
Thirty-one daily suites and two-hour scratch/burst budgets are assumptions, not schedules installed by this cost update.
The fixed 19 user/OKE VMs plus six managed database nodes remain continuously billed; benchmark pods use already-budgeted runner capacity.

Changing capacity, test frequency, retained datasets, backup duration or retention requires recalculating this budget. Configured gold snapshots and versioned buckets may grow beyond the first-month allowance.

benchmark_evidence.limitations: Transfer values are rounded upstream endpoint summaries, not OCI billing meters. Request count is derived from reported RPS and the 60-second profile. Same-region runner traffic is not assumed to be billable internet egress. No retained measurements establish database disk bytes, object bytes, backup size, backup duration or actual load-balancer billed bandwidth.

assumption_rationale.reason: One daily suite gives about 3.11 million benchmark requests and 450 GB of response data per month at the latest observed profile. Generator preparation, retries and ordinary Dev use need additional headroom. Keep the fixture roughly stable; repeated creation of fresh datasets without removal would accumulate data.

50 GiB for GitLab and 10 GiB for Praefect budget room for the 10,000-project/1,000-subgroup fixture, imported GitLab project, indexes, metadata and scenario writes. These are monthly average billable storage assumptions, not Terraform provisioned capacities.

Retain the original estimator assumption of 30 VPUs per storage GiB for the configured 75K IOPS tier. The precise managed PostgreSQL billing mapping remains unverified; 1500 and 300 VPU-GB-month are modeled, not measured.

512 GiB average comprises 128 GiB live/versioned application data, 256 GiB GitLab backup allowance (32 copies at 8 GiB), 64 GiB registry/packages and 64 GiB temporary staging. None is a measured footprint. The current configuration does not expire versions/backups at these budgets; costs grow without cleanup.

10 million requests/month leaves headroom above about 3.11 million monthly benchmark HTTP requests for storage operations, uploads, backup traffic and setup. GitLab HTTP requests do not map one-to-one to Object Storage operations.

1024 GiB of retained billable backup data across all three replicas allows for full/incremental snapshots and repository changes. Gold retention includes longer-lived snapshots, so this is a first-month Dev budget rather than a steady-state retention forecast.
Budget all 30 retained daily backups at the full combined assumed 60 GiB database size: 1800 GiB. Compression/incremental sharing and initial retention ramp-up may reduce actual billing.

The latest run reports an endpoint-average response rate near 912 Mbps. Budget both LBs at their 1000 Mbps maximum for two hours daily, covering the 84-minute suite plus margin; 100 Mbps minimum for the other 22 hours. This is 175 Mbps per LB as a monthly weighted average, not a configuration change.

1024 GB/month of external downloads, clones, artifacts and other Dev traffic. The approximately 450 GB monthly benchmark response data travels between same-region OCI resources and is not automatically treated as billed internet egress. No credit is taken for shared free allowances.

Two hours per daily backup gives 62 volume-hours for a 1024 GiB Balanced volume. Actual backup duration was not measured. Failed jobs or delayed PVC cleanup can increase allocation time; full-month scratch would add 39.89 USD.
